clue.text: Giving up time for pay, one's still working thus?

definitions.text: Giving up time for pay, one's still working thus?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged
giving up means the named letter is surrendered from the word still

explanation.surface: A wry question about someone who goes on working when they could simply stop, because they are paid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving up time' takes the T out of STILL to leave SILL; 'working' then rearranges FOR PAY ONE'S SILL. The whole clue also describes the answer: a paid worker who does it for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exchanges their hours for a wage, and carries on at a job, is doing it as a career rather than as a hobby.

clue.text: Centre's capital otherwise emulates landmark in Pisa?

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'
the famous tower of Pisa leans, so to copy it is to lean

explanation.surface: A trivia-style question about a central capital that behaves like the famous tower in Pisa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' looks like a general word for the middle, but it is the name of a French region, Centre-Val de Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city on the Loire is the administrative seat of the Centre-Val de Loire region.

clue.text: Different inertia-reel seat belts

indicators.note: belts here means wraps round, so the phrase holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A description of car seat belts with the reel mechanism that locks when you brake.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other or otherwise, as in 'someone else', so it matches different.

clue.text: Restrictive strap that keeps suit up

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the strap word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a sling is a strap or band that supports an injured arm

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to fit is to suit, as clothes do

explanation.surface: A tight strap that holds a suit of clothes in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifling describes something oppressive that smothers and holds back, so it is a synonym for restrictive.

clue.text: Speaker's prevailed, to evaluate not allowing debate?

indicators.note: the speaker's version is what is heard, so the words are spelt as they sound

parts.note: won means prevailed and to weigh up is to evaluate; said together they are heard as WON WEIGH

explanation.surface: Suggests the Speaker of the House has won, judging a motion and allowing no debate on it.
explanation.definitionFit: One-way communication runs in only a single direction, with no reply or argument permitted.

clue.text: John erected surrounding houses with unresolved issues

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the word for surrounding takes the other piece in

parts.note: ambient means surrounding, as in ambient temperature

indicators.note: erected means set upright, and in a down clue that reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is lav, short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A man called John put up houses around something and left matters unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a person's name but is the slang word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ambivalent means having mixed feelings and being unable to decide, so the person's issues stay unresolved.

clue.text: Cat embracing sloth's a thing

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the big cat wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
the ai is a three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite; with 's it gives AIS

explanation.surface: A zoo-like picture of a big cat hugging a sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A thing' is slang for a romantic affair, and an affair is also called a liaison.

clue.text: Editor's pitched into recurring case of Lane's attraction of Kent

indicators.note: into means the following letters go inside the repeated outer pair

parts.note: the case of Lane is its outer letters LE, and recurring means it appears twice
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor, plus S for the 's
cast means pitched or thrown

explanation.surface: Evokes Superman's editor being thrown into the story with Lois Lane and the attraction of Clark Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Lane and Kent call up Lois Lane and Clark Kent from Superman, but Kent is the English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This moated castle near Maidstone is one of the best-known tourist sights in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Aromatic fruit, first of lotus species found in Australian town

indicators.note: found in means these letters sit inside the town's name

parts.note: Alice Springs, known as Alice, is a town in central Australia

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of lotus

parts.note: sp. is the standard abbreviation for species

explanation.surface: A botanical note about a lotus species growing in an outback town.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is the dried berry of a West Indian tree, used as a fragrant spice, so it is an aromatic fruit.

clue.text: Pull up dense undergrowth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to slow down or stop
second meaning: a thicket of bushes or bracken

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense, a thicket, is the same word as bracken and is uncommon outside older English.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stopping a vehicle and an area thick with shrubs.

clue.text: Monstrous glove clutches note enclosing request

indicators.note: clutches means grips, so the glove holds the following piece inside

parts.note: a mitten is a glove without separate fingers

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the note goes round the request

parts.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
to beg is to request

explanation.surface: A picture of a glove gripping a note that contains a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Misbegotten means badly conceived or illegitimate, and it is used for something grotesque or hideous.

clue.text: One is welcoming muezzin's prologue?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the phrase holds the other letter inside

parts.note: said by oneself, one is becomes I AM

indicators.note: a prologue is the opening part, so take the first letter of muezzin

explanation.surface: Describes a mosque leader greeting the muezzin's call to prayer that comes before the service.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the leader of prayers who follows the muezzin's call.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque, after the muezzin has called the faithful to come.

clue.text: Exotic ivies'll add rash

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's warning that foreign ivy plants will cause a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' reads as a skin complaint caused by ivy, but here it is the adjective meaning hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is reckless and unwise, so it is badly thought out.

clue.text: Gabby Logan's article is replaced by rehashed timeless rhetoric

indicators.note: is replaced by means the article in the name is dropped so other letters can take its place

parts.note: the name Logan is used as it is written
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rehashed means reworked, so the letters are rearranged
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Suggests the TV presenter Gabby Logan being replaced by a speaker of reworked rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gabby' looks like the first name of Gabby Logan, the British sports presenter, but it is the definition. RHETORIC loses its T to give RHEORIC, which is rearranged as ORRHEIC to take the place of AN in LOGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Logorrhoea is an excessive flow of words, so a logorrheic person is talkative to a fault.

clue.text: Bulrushes in prime place once driving out area's reeds

indicators.note: in prime place means the letter at the very front of Bulrushes
driving out means the named letter is expelled from the phrase

parts.note: as soon as means once, as in 'once you arrive, call me'
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Sounds like a nature note about bulrushes growing in a favoured spot before the area's reeds are pushed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeds' seems to be more plants beside the bulrushes, but here it means reed instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoon is a woodwind instrument played with a double reed, and musicians call such instruments reeds.

clue.text: Instructive meeting where commander-in-chief holds nothing back

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the abbreviation takes the reversed word inside
back means the word for nothing is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A briefing where the commander-in-chief keeps nothing secret from his officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic can be a teaching session, such as a coaching clinic where experts teach a skill.

clue.text: Care of a delicate fabric fringing fine exposed seam

parts.note: c/o, CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: fringing means the fabric word borders the abbreviation, taking it in

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sewing instruction about a fine lace edging on an exposed seam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed seam' looks like dressmaking but is mining: a seam of coal laid bare for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: In a mine, the coal face is the surface of the seam that is uncovered and worked by the miners.

clue.text: Work to rule grand city in the North West

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
Oslo is the capital of Norway, in northern Europe
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Seems to describe ruling a grand city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is industrial action in which staff deliberately work slowly, much like strictly following every regulation.

clue.text: America in turn uncovered answer for smaller region

indicators.note: in turn means the abbreviation is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: bare means uncovered

explanation.surface: Suggests America in its turn exposing the answer about a smaller region.
explanation.definitionFit: A subarea is a portion or subdivision of a larger area, so it is a lesser zone within it.

clue.text: Money order frees police force up

definitions.note: the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are a force 'up' on horseback, hence the nickname

parts.note: unties means frees

explanation.surface: Reads like a bribe: a money order that gets the police to free someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, a force that historically patrolled on horseback.

clue.text: Resisting disturbance from the south, island on western part of UK

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
re means on or concerning
NI, Northern Ireland, is the western part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Sounds like a report of an island off the western UK coast resisting a storm from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in its motion, so it opposes a disturbance.

clue.text: Head off over the hill after fancy motor's nicked

indicators.note: after means the trimmed word comes behind the car's name

parts.note: a Jag, short for Jaguar, is a luxury car

indicators.note: head off means remove the first letter

parts.note: aged means old, over the hill

explanation.surface: A car thief steals a fancy motor and heads off over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' reads as British slang for stolen, but here it means notched or cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A jagged edge has sharp cuts and notches along it, so it is nicked.

clue.text: Host's bread holder needs pill before eating salt

parts.note: tab is short for tablet, a pill

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the word for before swallows the formula

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: A host's bread bin needs a pill taken before eating salty food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person giving a dinner, but here it is the consecrated bread of the Eucharist.
explanation.definitionFit: In churches, the tabernacle is the ornamented cupboard where the consecrated wafers are reserved.

clue.text: Despicable English will come sooner or later in disguise

indicators.note: will come sooner says the letter moves forward in the word; 'or later' allows the other spelling, EVIL, with it moving back

parts.note: vile means despicable

explanation.surface: A warning that something despicable in England will always surface eventually under its mask.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting from VILE the E moves earlier; starting from EVIL, also despicable, it moves later, which is why the clue says 'sooner or later'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil hides the face, so it serves as a covering or cloak to hide things.

clue.text: Suit used by fortune-teller dismissing core transitions in zodiac

indicators.note: dismissing core means the central letter of the word is thrown out

parts.note: a cusp is the point where one zodiac sign passes into the next

explanation.surface: An astrologer ignoring the key changeovers between signs while reading fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: In a tarot deck, which fortune-tellers use for readings, one of the four suits is cups.

clue.text: Perpetually expressed in poetry that is like Poe's

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A comment that the poems of Edgar Allan Poe are always phrased in a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe wrote tales and poems of the uncanny, so his work is famously spooky.

clue.text: Snitch collared by criminal that hasn't left tip

indicators.note: collared by means held round the neck, so the trimmed word goes around the informer
hasn't means the named letter is missing from the word for criminal

parts.note: guilty means criminal, culpable
a rat is an informer, a snitch

explanation.surface: An informer is arrested by a crook who has not left a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' reads as a stingy crook not tipping, but it is the definition, a gift of money to a waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity is money given for service on top of a bill, which is a tip.

clue.text: Spread by dancers falls when they wear masks

definitions.note: the event at which guests wear masks, a noun phrase for the occasion

indicators.note: spread means scattered, so the letters are dispersed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A spread laid on by dancers who fall about while wearing masks.
explanation.definitionFit: At a costume party guests dress up, often with masks, so it is the occasion of masked dancing.
